title: Channel
description: One researched venue where a specific audience already gathers, produced by an audience and channel research pass (see CHANNELS.md). A channels file is a JSON array of these objects. The defining requirement is `rules`: every venue carries a verbatim quote of what its own rules page says about self-promotion, the URL that quote came from, and the date it was read. A channel without a verified or explicitly unverified rules block is not a recommendation, because the failure mode this schema exists to prevent is getting banned somewhere you were told you were welcome.

url.description: Where the reader goes to act: the submission form, the inclusion policy, the forum itself.

class.description: placement: a directory or index the thing sits in and gets found. earned: a human with an audience chooses to cover you. participation: somewhere the audience talks and you are one of the people talking. Paid placement is deliberately out of scope.

cadence.description: one_time entries form the placement checklist you grind once per project. recurring entries form the standing watchlist and MUST carry a trigger.

effort.description: Effort is the primary sorting axis of this method, not cost. A reader with one free afternoon and a reader with twenty minutes a day need different answers.

hours.description: Realistic hands-on time, as a range: "0.25", "1-2", "4-8". Per occurrence for recurring channels.

time_to_first_result.description: Elapsed time between acting and anything visible happening ("1-2 weeks", "up to 3 months"). Strongly preferred. Without it a reader reads normal latency as failure and quits early.

rules.description: What this venue's own rules page says about self-promotion. The anchor of the whole method. Never fill this from memory or inference.

verdict.description: open_door: explicitly invites maker submissions. conditional: allowed within a stated limit or ratio. closed: banned outright, or banned for this commercial category. unwritten: the rules were read and say nothing about promotion, which is the HIGHEST risk state, not the lowest, because the rule exists in habit and is enforced without a page to point at. unverified: the rules page could not be opened, so this is a task for the reader and not a recommendation.

rules_url.description: The exact page the quote was read on. Required whenever verdict is not unverified.

quote.description: Verbatim sentences from the rules page about self-promotion. Not a paraphrase. Required whenever the verdict is open_door, conditional, or closed.

checked.description: The date the page was actually read, as a real calendar day. Rules pages change, and a reader needs to know how stale this is. The pattern rejects impossible months and days. It cannot catch 2026-02-31, so anything validating this file should check the date parses too.

open_source_carveout.description: Verbatim text where a venue bans commercial promotion but permits sharing free or open source work. Worth its own field because it is the door most people never notice, and because it turns a closed verdict into an open one for an MIT or GPL project.

hard_gates.description: Requirements that disqualify a project outright before any time is spent: license restrictions, minimum age since first release, no-proprietary-dependency rules, required documentation or demo. Belongs at the top of a rendered entry, because a gate the reader fails makes the rest irrelevant.

audience_evidence.description: Why this venue is believed to be alive and to contain the target audience, citing something dated that was actually seen on the page. A venue that sounds right and is dead is worse than no venue, because it spends the time budget for nothing.

trigger.description: Required for cadence=recurring. The event in the world that means it is time to act ("when you ship a release with a user-visible change", "when someone asks for a tool that does X"). Must never be a frequency: "post monthly" is a content calendar, and it decays into posting because of the date rather than because there is something to say.

ban_risk.description: The specific local tripwire that gets an account banned here, taken from the rules that were actually read. Not generic advice.

pros.description: This method returns pros and cons per venue, never a ranking. A ranked list invites the reader to do number one and stop, which is the behavior that gets people banned from number one.

cons.description: Required, and non-empty. A venue with no listed downside means it was not looked at hard enough.

disclosure.description: How the maker identifies themselves when acting here, phrased as part of the action rather than as a footnote. The guardrail in CHANNELS.md is that producing landscape is fine and manufacturing a source never is, so every recommended action carries its own disclosure.

allOf.$comment: `unwritten` is also a claim about a page that was read: it asserts the rules were checked and said nothing about promotion. That owes a URL and a date like any other reading, and only the quote is excused, because there is nothing to quote. Without this, a bare {"verdict": "unwritten"} is valid and a verified absence is indistinguishable from a guess. The distinction matters more here than anywhere else in the schema, since both skills tell readers to treat `unwritten` as the highest-risk verdict. `unverified` requires neither, because it claims the opposite: no page was read, and sometimes no rules page could even be found.
